newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LEONARD NOT AFRAID LOSS WOULD BLACKEN CAREER.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LEONARD NOT AFRAID LOSS WOULD BLACKEN CAREER.

text.p: Sugar Ray Leonard is not afraid that a loss in his comeback fight against Hector "Macho" Camacho next month would blacken his career.

"I don't think one fight, one performance can tarnish one's reputation," Leonard said in a telephone press conference Thursday from Scottsdale, Arizona, where he has been training for the March 1 fight at the Atlantic City Convention Centre. It will be his first fight in six years.

"People remember you as they want to and I would like to be remembered as having made an impact and having been gracious as a winner or loser," said the 40-year-old Leonard, a world champion in five different weight classes and a gold medal winner in the 1976 Olympics.
Unfortunately, Leonard left people with an unforgettable last memory when he was badly beaten by Terry Norris on February 1, 1991, before retiring with a 36-2-1 record,.
"I'm a perfectionist and it bothered me," Leonard said of the pounding he took from Norris.

While Leonard is reported to be getting a $5 million purse for challenging Camacho (63-3-1), the holder of the lightly regarded International Boxing Council middleweight crown, he says it is not the money that has brought him back.
"Ninty-nine point nine percent of fighters come back for financial gain. That is not necessarily the case for me," Leonard said.

"It is something people find difficult to understand, but this is what I've done for all those years and this is like going back to an old job," said Leonard. "This is something I know I can do and I will do."
He said he would not rule out another bout after this one, but did rule out making it a regular occurrence.
"After March 1st I will look at it, but you've got to be realistic, I'm 40 years old, or should I say young, and I know I'm not coming back for a career," Leonard said.
